analysis: The supplied units are CHANGELOG.md head-text excerpts only (lines 222-602). No source code, tests, or configuration were provided, so the behavior the entries describe cannot be verified. Entries relevant to the threat model: (1) Frozen legacy MDM cohort and /v1/enroll gating (lines 286-297), TB-009/TB-011, T-036, T-052. They require qualified App Attest for noncohort serving and base rewards, and acknowledge that copied generic profiles can still enroll directly in MicroMDM. The threat-model comments already cover this. (2) Removal of caller-supplied user/metadata/safety_identifier/prompt_cache_key from provider-bound bodies (line 268), T-003/T-051. Consistent with the existing 'does not anonymize prompt content' note. (3) Removal of the unauthenticated /v1/provider/earnings wallet lookup (line 560), which closes T-031. (4) Fail-closed attestation challenges, protocol-3-only App Attest, and a provider version floor that excludes missing versions (lines 556, 562, 564). These tighten T-033/T-036/T-053. (5) Removal of ACME/Python-era fields and the telemetry events route. (6) The SSD prefix-cache TTL raise to 30 minutes and the write budget raise to 750GB/day (lines 501-503, 585). The changelog says the TTL raise was recorded as a SEC-035 re-acceptance, but the T-041 detail was not supplied, so whether the threat model reflects the 750GB/day budget cannot be confirmed. This relates to T-041/T-016. (7) Cache routing persistence (lines 460-466) stores holders and demand across restarts and persists no prompts or raw chain hashes. That is a possible T-041 timing/oracle interaction, and the persistence of cross-tenant cache state needs source review. (8) Cache-credit near-tie routing preference (line 596) and demand-gated SSD writes (line 586) relate to the T-041 oracle. No concrete security regression is evidenced by documentation text alone. Next passes should check the corresponding code in coordinator/internal/provider/legacymdm, the enrollment handler, cache routing persistence, and provider-body minimization.
